answer: A decentralized proof-of-burn registry imposes superlinear cost scaling to prevent Sybil attacks: an agent wishing to register identity clusters across the network must burn cryptographic collateral at a cost scaling as O(n²). The required burnt tokens decompose like brittle shale into unrecoverable umber ash, transforming the verified pool into a secure oasis where forging multiple identities incurs prohibitive exponential losses.
